strings.name: Paul Krugman
strings.role: Economist · International trade and economic geography
strings.summary: Paul Krugman studies economies of scale, product differentiation and spatial concentration, explaining trade between similar countries and why industries cluster. His work advanced new trade theory and new economic geography and earned the 2008 economics Nobel. His public writing addresses crises, fiscal policy and inequality; scholarship and political commentary should be assessed separately.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. The timeline ends with his 2024 departure from the New York Times; current university and author information was checked. Political commentary is not academic consensus.
strings.influence.rationale: Influential for new trade theory and economic geography, alongside sustained public economic commentary.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: New trade theory
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Explained trade between similar economies through scale economies and demand for product variety.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Geography and public writing
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Studied the location of economic activity and explained macroeconomics and policy debates to general readers.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Ends New York Times column
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Ended the column begun in 2000 and continued writing on his own platform.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Moves to CUNY
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Left full-time teaching at Princeton and joined CUNY’s research community.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Economics Nobel
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Recognized for research on trade patterns and the location of economic activity.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Princeton and newspaper commentary
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Joined Princeton while beginning sustained public commentary on economic policy.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: New economic geography
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Published a theory of industrial clustering and received the John Bates Clark Medal.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: New trade-theory paper
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Explained trade patterns using economies of scale and product variety.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: MIT doctorate
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Completed his economics PhD, taught at Yale and subsequently at MIT and other institutions.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Born in New York State
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Born in Albany and raised on Long Island; graduated from Yale in 1974.
